title: The `EMMA` User's Guide
text: Functional Enrichment Analysis (FEA) key downstream step omics workflows, commonly applied differential expression analysis support biological interpretation generate pathway-level hypotheses. wide range tools methods available, mainly -Representation Analysis (ORA) (Khatri et al. 2012) doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1002375 Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) (Subramanian et al. 2005) doi:10.1073/pnas.0506580102, leading substantial heterogeneity analytical choices reported results. Despite widespread use, FEA often insufficiently documented (Wijesooriya et al. 2022) doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1009935. Critical parameters background gene sets multiple testing correction methods frequently missing inconsistently reported scientific papers, limiting reproducibility interpretability. Currently, standardized framework exists ensure transparent reproducible documentation FEA workflows, comparable MIAME guidelines (Brazma et al. 2001) doi:10.1038/ng1201-365. address gap, introduce EMMA, framework automatically captures key analytical parameters provenance information execution FEA methods. vignette demonstrates EMMA integrates existing tools (e.g. clusterProfiler, topGO, Enrichr, gprofiler2) execute enrichment analyses systematically capturing analysis parameters provenance information runtime, returning enrichment results without altering original format, alongside structured reusable metadata.
